sn48.42:1.2: Uṇṇābha became a lay follower following a discussion on the bases of psychic power at SN 51.15. He was evidently named for his “woolly eyebrows”.
sn48.42:2.1: The phrasing here parallels the simile of the six animals in SN 35.247. Here, however, the text makes it clear that we are talking about meditative development, as is also the case where the same phrase appears in MN 43:21.3.
sn48.42:3.4: In terms of meditative progress, the five faculties imply sense restraint as a preparation for meditation. Then one withdraws from the senses to that which is their center and controller, the mind. Mindfulness then leads to the liberation of immersion, culminating in awakening.
sn48.42:4.4: “Freedom” is identified with the faculty of samādhi at SN 48.46:2.7.
sn48.42:6.5: That is, he is a non-returner.
